title: autotune: sensible defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token cost and operational friction by providing conservative, workload-aware defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, introduce recommended quantization profiles for common model families, and ship a small unit-economics CLI to evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs. This PR bundles three related deliverables into a single rollout to make it easy for customers to opt-in or for Dedicated clusters to pick defaults. Changes: - runtime: new autotune/defaults module that computes batching window, max_batch_size, and cache TTL based on observed latency percentiles and request size distribution - cache: smarter prefix/KV cache heuristics (hot-key detection, adaptive TTL) - quant: add quant profiles (int8/4bit) for Llama2, Mistral-like, and Vicuna families with metadata for compatible kernels - tooling: unit_econ CLI and API endpoint to estimate tokens-per-second, cost-per-1M-tokens, and expected latency under different profiles - config: add feature flag redwood.autotune.defaults and per-customer override path - docs: new docs page and rollout checklist - tests: new unit and integration tests and perf canary harness updates Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind redwood.autotune.defaults; staged canary to 5% traffic with automatic rollback on latency regressions >2p50 or error-rate >0.5%. Related: ENG-4281 (autotune engine), ENG-4310 (quant registry), PM-102 (cost optimization initiative).

release_notes: Sane autotune defaults for batching and KV caching, recommended quantization profiles for common models, and a unit-economics tooling CLI to estimate cost/latency. Feature-flagged behind redwood.autotune.defaults; disabled by default for Dedicated until customer opt-in.
additional_context: This PR consolidates several tickets to make testing and rollout consistent. The defaults are conservative by design and include telemetry tags so we can measure adoption and regressions. The unit_econ tool is intentionally read-only and does not change runtime behavior unless used to generate config suggestions.
